language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.
language.lessonRating: How do you feel about this exercise?

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
G-day! I’m Ellie! I live in Australia. Do you see this? This is a truck stop. My father and mother work here.
People come here if they want to put gas in their car or if they want something to eat or drink. There’s always something to do here, lots of people and cars!
I’m helping my father today. Do you want to join me? I have to add up all kinds of things today: trucks, cars and candy.
I’ll tell you how this works: adding up is putting things together. For example: when you have one truck and you add two other trucks, then you have three trucks.
It goes like this, you see: one truck, and another is two, and another makes three. You can help yourself count if you use your fingers or some little stones or pebbles.
If you have to add up one and two, you can count on your hands. One, plus another one, plus another one, and that makes.... Right, three! Very good!
For adding up we use this sign a ‘plus’. Plus means add up. And you can add up everything: trucks, cars or candy... And that is what we’re gonna do.
Shall we do another example? You see Wally here? He is a kangaroo. He has four sisters. So how many kangaroo children are there in his family?
We can find this out by adding up. Wally’s one kangaroo, and then add up four kangaroo’s, which makes one plus four, is five! So there are five kangaroo children in his family.
To show the answer to a sum, so in this case how many kangaroo children there are in Wally’s family, we use the ‘=‘ sign. That means ‘after this comes the answer’.
